s:
Consider the following statements regarding prison administration in India:
1. 'Prisons / persons detained therein' is Entry 4 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.
2. The Prisons Act, 1894 kept prisons with the Union Government, which alone frames prison rules.
3. The Model Prisons Act, 2023 prepared by the MHA is binding on all States.
4. The BPR&D issues advisory guidelines on prison administration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 1894 Act kept prisons with the Provincial (now State) Governments, which make the rules. 3 is wrong: the Model Prisons Act 2023 is only a guide for States to replace the 1894 Act; it is not binding.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding NCRB Prison Statistics 2024:
1. India had 1,333 prisons, with inmates exceeding the capacity.
2. The occupancy rate was 112.7%, the highest being in Meghalaya.
3. Undertrials made up about 73% of the inmates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct (1,333 prisons, ~4.53 lakh capacity vs 5.11 lakh inmates; ~73% undertrials). 2 is wrong: occupancy was 112.7% but the highest was Delhi (194.6%); Meghalaya was second (163.5%).

s:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Principle):
List-I (Case) | List-II (Principle)
a. Nilabati Behera (1993) | i. Arrest memo, officer identification and medical check
b. Joginder Kumar (1994) | ii. Compensation for custodial death; no sovereign immunity
c. D.K. Basu (1997) | iii. No automatic arrest for offences punishable up to 7 years
d. Arnesh Kumar (2014) | iv. Arrest must be justified; a friend or relative to be informed
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Nilabati Behera – compensation under Arts 32/226, no sovereign immunity; Joginder Kumar – arrest must be justified; D.K. Basu – arrest safeguards (memo, ID, informing kin, medical check); Arnesh Kumar – no automatic arrest for offences up to 7 years (CrPC s.41, now BNSS s.35).

s:
Consider the following statements regarding custodial deaths:
1. A judicial inquiry into a custodial death, mandatory under CrPC s.176(1A), is now under BNSS s.196.
2. Between 1999 and 2023 there were 2,253 police-custody deaths but only 3 convictions, most deaths being in Uttar Pradesh.
3. BNSS s.218 requires sanction before a court takes cognisance against a public servant.
4. The Gade Sai Krishna custodial death in Andhra Pradesh involved the Krishnalanka police of Visakhapatnam.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: most police-custody deaths were in Bihar. 4 is wrong: Krishnalanka police station is in Vijayawada.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding encounter and custodial deaths:
1. PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines on encounter killings.
2. Under these guidelines an out-of-turn promotion may be given to the officers once the NHRC is informed.
3. An encounter death is to be independently probed by the CID, with a magisterial inquiry.
4. NHRC norms require a custodial death to be reported to it within 48 hours.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: no out-of-turn promotion or gallantry award until the officers are cleared. 4 is wrong: NHRC norms require reporting within 24 hours, with post-mortem videography and independent investigation.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding police reforms:
1. Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006) issued seven directives on police reform.
2. The DGP is to be chosen from a UPSC panel and given a minimum tenure of three years.
3. The State Police Complaints Authority is headed by a retired IAS officer.
4. The Police Act, 1861 is still in force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the DGP gets a 2-year tenure. 3 is wrong: the State PCA is headed by a retired judge.

s:
Match List-I (Body) with List-II (Focus):
List-I (Body) | List-II (Focus)
a. Mulla Committee (1980-83) | i. Abolish death penalty except terrorism and waging war
b. Krishna Iyer Committee (1987) | ii. Prison overcrowding and undertrials
c. Amitava Roy Committee (2018) | iii. Women prisoners and women in police
d. 262nd Law Commission (2015) | iv. All India Prison Service
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Mulla – jail reforms, All India Prison Service; Krishna Iyer – women prisoners, women in police; Amitava Roy – overcrowding and undertrials; 262nd Law Commission – abolition except terrorism and waging war.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India signed the UN Convention against Torture in 1997 but has not ratified it.
Reason (R): The 273rd Law Commission Report (2017) recommended ratifying UNCAT and drafted a Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true (notes: India signed UNCAT in 1997, not ratified; 273rd LC recommended ratification with a draft Bill 2017). R does not explain A: a recommendation to ratify is not the reason ratification has not happened.

s:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Holding):
List-I (Case) | List-II (Holding)
a. Jagmohan Singh (1973) | i. Pardon open to limited judicial review
b. Machhi Singh (1983) | ii. Death penalty constitutional
c. Epuru Sudhakar (2006) | iii. Inordinate delay in mercy justifies commutation
d. Shatrughan Chauhan (2014) | iv. Categories; aggravating vs mitigating factors
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Jagmohan Singh – death penalty constitutional; Machhi Singh – categories, aggravating vs mitigating; Epuru Sudhakar – limited judicial review of pardon; Shatrughan Chauhan – inordinate delay in mercy → commute.

s:
With reference to Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014), consider the following statements:
1. Inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition can justify commuting death to life imprisonment.
2. At least 7 days' notice must be given before execution after a mercy petition is rejected.
3. Solitary confinement of death-row convicts was held illegal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Court required 14 days' notice before execution.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the death sentence in India:
1. A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by the High Court.
2. Under Article 161 the Governor can pardon a death sentence.
3. An appeal can reach the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.
4. Murder (old IPC s.302) is now punished under BNS s.101.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: under Art. 161 the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence (may commute/remit/suspend); only the President can under Art. 72. 4 is wrong: murder is now BNS s.103.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Amnesty International's data on executions:
1. China is the world's biggest executioner.
2. Executions were carried out in 23 countries in 2017.
3. At least 2,707 executions (excluding China) were recorded in 2025, the highest since 1981.
4. Saudi Arabia carried out the most recorded executions in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: Iran led the recorded executions in 2025.

s:

x: Rammohan Roy – Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin; Vidyasagar – Bethune School 1849 (and the Widow Remarriage Act 1856); Jyotirao Phule – Gulamgiri; Pandita Ramabai – The High-Caste Hindu Woman (1887).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule started the first girls' school at Pune in 1848.
2. Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.
3. Kandukuri Veeresalingam performed the first Telugu widow remarriage at Rajahmundry in 1891.
4. The Phules opened a home to prevent infanticide in 1863.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Veeresalingam performed the first Telugu widow remarriage at Rajahmundry in 1881, not 1891.

s:
Match List-I (Work / organisation) with List-II (Person):

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Stri Purush Tulana – Tarabai Shinde; The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna – Mahendranath Gupta ('M'); Sambad Kaumudi – Rammohan Roy; Arya Mahila Samaj (1882) – Pandita Ramabai.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the status of women in Indian history:
1. In the Vedic period the wife was honoured as 'Ardhangini'.
2. Purdah became prominent in the Rig Vedic period.
3. Niyoga was a custom that banned widow remarriage.
4. The Devadasi system was banned in Andhra Pradesh by both the Madras Act 1947 and the AP Act 1988.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: purdah became prominent in the later Vedic and medieval periods. 3 is wrong: Niyoga let a childless widow/wife have a son by the husband's brother or kinsman; it was not a ban on widow remarriage.

s:
Match List-I (Act) with List-II (Year):
List-I (Act) | List-II (Year)
a. Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act | i. 2006
b. Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act | ii. 1986
c. PCPNDT Act | iii. 1994
d. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act | iv. 1987
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Indecent Representation of Women Act – 1986 (ads, publications, paintings – not child marriage); Commission of Sati (Prevention) – 1987; PCPNDT – 1994; Prohibition of Child Marriage – 2006 (replaced the Sarda Act 1929).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Muslims.
2. The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 bans giving, taking and demanding dowry.
3. The Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is a civil remedy that provides a Right to Residence under Section 17.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Indian Succession Act 1925 covers Christians and others, not Muslims.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The PCPNDT Act, 1994 came into force on 1 January 1994.
2. The PCPNDT Act bans prenatal sex determination.
3. The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 replaced the Sarda Act and fixes 18 years for females and 21 for males.
4. The POSH Act, 2013 requires an Internal Committee at workplaces with 10 or more employees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the PCPNDT Act of 1994 came into force on 1 January 1996.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding personal laws:
1. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a civil, secular marriage irrespective of religion, after public notice.
2. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy, grounds of divorce and restitution of conjugal rights.
3. Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners in 1995, after the national amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: AP's HSA amendment came in 1985 under N.T. Rama Rao – before the national HSA (Amendment) 2005.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In October 2025 the Supreme Court upheld the exclusion of Scheduled Tribes from the Hindu Succession Act.
Reason (R): Section 2(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 excludes members of notified Scheduled Tribes from its application.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: s.2(2) of the HSA excludes notified STs (unless the Centre directs otherwise), and the SC (8 Oct 2025) upheld that exclusion.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares instant talaq-e-biddat void and illegal.
2. Pronouncing instant talaq under the 2019 Act is punishable with imprisonment up to five years.
3. The maintenance remedy of Section 125 CrPC is now Section 144 of the BNSS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 2019 Act provides imprisonment up to three years.

s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Content):
List-I (Article) | List-II (Content)
a. Article 15(3) | i. Renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
b. Article 39(d) | ii. Equal pay for equal work
c. Article 44 | iii. Special provisions for women and children
d. Article 51A(e) | iv. Uniform Civil Code
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 15(3) – special provisions for women and children; 39(d) – equal pay for equal work; 44 – UCC; 51A(e) – renounce practices derogatory to women's dignity.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation for women:
1. Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts in Panchayats.
2. Article 243T provides the same for Municipalities.
3. Articles 330A and 332A reserve one-half of the seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
4. The 106th Amendment quota in the Lok Sabha awaits the Census and delimitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Arts 330A/332A (106th Amendment, 2023) reserve one-third of the seats.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 106th Amendment's women's quota came into effect in the J&K and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
2. The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was passed on 17 April 2026.
3. About 46% of PRI representatives are women (January 2026).
4. Andhra Pradesh reserves one-third of seats in panchayats and municipalities for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated on 17 April 2026. 4 is wrong: AP reserves 50% in panchayats and municipalities (and 50% of nominated posts and work contracts).

List-I (Case) | List-II (Ruling)
a. Sarla Mudgal (1995) | i. Conversion cannot validate a second Hindu marriage
b. Vishaka (1997) | ii. Struck down s.497 IPC (adultery)
c. Seema v Ashwani Kumar (2006) | iii. Compulsory registration of marriages
d. Joseph Shine (2018) | iv. Workplace harassment guidelines
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Sarla Mudgal – conversion to Islam cannot validate a second Hindu marriage; Vishaka – workplace harassment guidelines (→ POSH 2013); Seema – compulsory marriage registration; Joseph Shine – s.497 struck down.

s:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Ruling):
List-I (Case) | List-II (Ruling)
a. Vineeta Sharma (2020) | i. Permanent commission for women SSC officers
b. Babita Puniya (2020) | ii. Abortion up to 24 weeks regardless of marital status
c. X v GNCTD (2022) | iii. Maternity protection covers post, status and promotion
d. Rakhi Bisht (Delhi HC, 2026) | iv. Daughter a coparcener by birth
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Vineeta Sharma – daughter coparcener by birth whether or not the father was alive on 9 Sept 2005; Babita Puniya – permanent commission (Army); X v GNCTD – 24 weeks for all women; Rakhi Bisht – maternity protection covers post, status, promotion.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Bano (1985) granted maintenance under Section 125 CrPC and was followed by the 1986 Act.
2. Danial Latifi (2001) limited a divorced Muslim wife's maintenance to the iddat period.
3. Shayara Bano (2017) held instant triple talaq unconstitutional by a 4:1 majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Danial Latifi held maintenance extends beyond iddat, for her whole life. 3 is wrong: the Shayara Bano majority was 3:2.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding women and places of worship:
1. In Sabarimala (2018) the bar on women aged 10-50 was struck down by a 4:1 majority.
2. Bindu Ammini and Kanaka Durga were the first women of that age to enter after the verdict (January 2019).
3. The Haji Ali Dargah case was decided by the Kerala High Court in 2016.
4. The Haji Ali petition was filed by the Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Haji Ali case (inner sanctum entry) was decided by the Bombay High Court in 2016.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding women's commissions:
1. The National Commission for Women was set up in January 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990.
2. The NCW is a constitutional body.
3. Besides the Chairperson and Member-Secretary, the NCW has five members, at least one each from the SCs and STs.
4. The A.P. Women's Commission was set up under an Act of 1998.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the NCW is a statutory body (NCW Act 1990), not a constitutional one. The AP commission (Act 1998) is chaired by Rayapati Sailaja (Dec 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Policy for Empowerment of Women was adopted in 2001, the Year of Women's Empowerment.
2. The Eighth Plan shifted the approach to women from 'development' to 'empowerment'.
3. The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016 placed food security and nutrition under the economy.
4. The Mission for Empowerment of Women was launched in 2010 and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao in 2015.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Draft Policy 2016 placed food security and nutrition under health.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Family Courts Act was enacted in 1984.
2. About 593 Family Courts were functioning as of 31 July 2025.
3. India's first exclusive women's court was set up at Malda in 2013.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: 953 Family Courts were functioning as of 31 July 2025.

s:

List-I (Milestone) | List-II (Year)
a. Commission on the Status of Women (under ECOSOC) | i. 1979
b. UN Decade for Women begins | ii. 1976
c. CEDAW adopted | iii. 1995
d. Beijing Fourth World Conference | iv. 1946
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CSW under ECOSOC – 1946; UN Decade for Women – 1976-85; CEDAW – 1979 (India signed 1980, ratified 1993); Beijing (4th) – 1995. Copenhagen was 1980, Nairobi 1985.

s:

List-I (Organisation) | List-II (Year of founding)
a. Bharat Stree Mahamandal | i. 1910
b. Women's Indian Association | ii. 1937
c. National Council of Women in India | iii. 1925
d. Andhra Mahila Sabha | iv. 1917
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal – 1910 (first women's organisation); WIA – 1917; NCWI – 1925; Andhra Mahila Sabha – 1937 (Durgabai Deshmukh).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Women's Indian Association (1917) was founded by Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins, among others.
2. Margaret Cousins founded the All India Women's Conference (1927), working on education, social upliftment and legal rights.
3. Durgabai Deshmukh was the first chairperson of the Central Social Welfare Board (1953).
4. In the early 20th century the women's movement shifted its focus to economic rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: in the early 20th century the focus shifted to political rights.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Committee on the Status of Women in India:
1. It was constituted in 1971 with Phulrenu Guha as chairperson.
2. Its Member-Secretary was Neera Desai.
3. Its report was titled 'Towards Equality' (1974).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Member-Secretary was Vina Mazumdar; Neera Desai founded the first Women's Studies Centre at SNDT.

s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Associated with):
List-I (Person) | List-II (Associated with)
a. Neera Desai | i. CWDS
b. Vina Mazumdar | ii. Manushi
c. Madhu Kishwar | iii. High-Level Committee on the Status of Women (2012)
d. Pam Rajput | iv. First Women's Studies Centre, SNDT
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Neera Desai – SNDT Women's Studies Centre; Vina Mazumdar – CWDS; Madhu Kishwar – Manushi; Pam Rajput – High-Level Committee (2012).

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra:
1. The Anti-Arrack Movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta in Krishna district.
2. It led to a ban on arrack in 1993 and total prohibition in 1995.
3. Chalam's novel 'Stree' dealt with women's personal and sexual freedom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Dubagunta is in Nellore district.

s:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I (Term) | List-II (Meaning)
a. Patriarchy | i. Scale of 0 (equality) to 1 (worst)
b. Gender mainstreaming | ii. Men hold primary power and status
c. Gender audit | iii. Gender perspective in all policies, laws and institutions
d. Gender Inequality Index | iv. Check of policies, programmes and budgets for gender equality
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Patriarchy – men hold primary power; gender mainstreaming – gender perspective in all policies (Beijing 1995); gender audit – check of policies, programmes, institutions, budgets; GII – 0 equality to 1 worst.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding gender indices:
1. The Gender Development Index is a female-to-male ratio in health, education and command over resources.
2. Military expenditure is one of the dimensions of the WEF Global Gender Gap Index.
3. India ranked 131st of 148 in the Global Gender Gap Index 2025.
4. India ranked 128th of 177 in the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Gender Gap Index covers economy, education, health and politics, not military spending. 4 is wrong: India was 131st of 177.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding sex ratio and work:
1. The sex ratio rose from 991 in NFHS-4 to 1020 in NFHS-5.
2. The sex ratio at birth rose from 904 to 917 (2021-23).
3. Kerala and Tamil Nadu are the most male-skewed States in sex ratio.
4. Women's labour force participation rate was 37% in 2022-23.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the most male-skewed States are Haryana and Punjab.

s:
Match List-I (Statement) with List-II (Person):
List-I (Statement) | List-II (Person)
a. 'I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved' | i. B.R. Ambedkar
b. 'A bird cannot fly on one wing' | ii. Amartya Sen
c. 'To call woman the weaker sex is a libel' | iii. Swami Vivekananda
d. 'Missing women' | iv. Mahatma Gandhi
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Ambedkar – progress of a community by women's progress; Vivekananda – a bird cannot fly on one wing; Gandhi – weaker sex a libel; Amartya Sen – 'missing women'.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The MTP Act, 1971 came into force on 1 April 1972.
2. The MTP law allows 24 weeks for special categories and prohibits disclosing the woman's identity.
3. The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 permits commercial surrogacy by a close relative.
4. Under the Surrogacy Act a woman can act as a surrogate only once.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Surrogacy Act 2021 permits only altruistic surrogacy; commercial surrogacy is prohibited.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The ART (Regulation) Act, 2021 prohibits the sale of gametes.
Reason (R): The ART (Regulation) Act, 2021 permits sex-selective ART in registered clinics.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the ART Act 2021 prohibits sale of gametes. R is false: it prohibits sex-selective ART; only registered clinics/banks may offer ART.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961:
1. Dower (mahr) under Muslim personal law is excluded from the definition of dowry.
2. Demanding dowry (s.4) is punishable with six months to two years and a fine up to ₹10,000.
3. Under s.8A the burden of proof lies on the prosecution.
4. Dowry Prohibition Officers under s.8B are appointed by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: s.8A puts the burden of proof on the accused. 4 is wrong: Dowry Prohibition Officers are appointed by the State Government.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 are compoundable.
Reason (R): The 1986 amendment brought dowry death (IPC 304B, now BNS 80) and its presumption (Evidence Act 113B, now BSA 118) into the law.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: offences under the Act are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. R is true: the 1986 amendment added dowry death and its presumption.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the POSH Act, 2013:
1. Its full name is the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.
2. An Internal Committee is presided over by a senior woman employee, has one NGO member and at least half its members are women.
3. The Local Committee for workplaces with fewer than 10 employees is constituted by the State Women's Commission.
4. Showing pornography is itself a form of sexual harassment under the Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Local Committee is constituted at the district by the District Officer (for workplaces with fewer than 10 employees or complaints against the employer).

s:
Under the POSH Act, 2013, consider the following time limits:
1. A complaint is to be made within 3 months, extendable by another 3 months.
2. The inquiry is to be completed within 60 days.
3. The employer must act on the inquiry report within 60 days.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the inquiry must be completed within 90 days.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Domestic Violence Act, 2005:
1. It is a criminal law.
2. Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal/emotional and economic abuse.
3. Protection Officers are appointed by the Central Government; in AP they are DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs.
4. Reliefs under the Act are granted by a Magistrate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the DV Act is a civil law. 3 is wrong: Protection Officers are appointed by the State Government (in AP, DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs).

s:
Match List-I (Relief under the DV Act, 2005) with List-II (Section):
List-I (Relief) | List-II (Section)
a. Right to reside | i. Section 18
b. Protection order | ii. Section 17
c. Residence order | iii. Section 19
d. Monetary relief | iv. Section 20
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Right to reside – s.17; protection order – s.18; residence order – s.19; monetary relief – s.20 (custody s.21, compensation s.22).

s:

Consider the following statements regarding maternity benefit:
1. The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 gave 12 weeks' leave in establishments with 10 or more employees.
2. Under the 2017 amendment a woman with fewer than two children gets 26 weeks, of which at most 8 may be before delivery.
3. From the third child onwards the leave is 12 weeks.
4. A woman adopting a child below six months gets 12 weeks from the date of hand-over.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the 12 weeks for an adoptive mother apply to a child below three months (also 12 weeks for a commissioning mother).

Consider the following statements:
1. The 2017 amendment makes a crèche mandatory in establishments with 50 or more employees, with four visits a day.
2. Work from home after maternity leave is allowed by mutual agreement.
3. The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes the Maternity Benefit Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Code on Wages subsumes the Equal Remuneration, Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Bonus Acts – not the Maternity Benefit Act.

Consider the following statements regarding trafficking:
1. The CLA 2013 definition of trafficking applies irrespective of the victim's consent.
2. UNODC identifies India and Pakistan as high destination countries.
3. In the US TIP Report, Tier 2 is the only tier fully meeting the minimum standards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Tier 1 is the only tier fully meeting the minimum standards (then Tier 2, Tier 2 Watch List, Tier 3).

Consider the following statements:
1. Under BNS s.124 an acid attack carries a minimum of 10 years up to life; an attempt, 5-7 years.
2. The presumption of dowry death is now in Section 118 of the BSA.
3. The BNS, BNSS and BSA came into force on 1 July 2023.
4. Laxmi v Union of India (2013) fixed compensation for acid-attack victims at a minimum of ₹1 lakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the new codes came into force on 1 July 2024. 4 is wrong: Laxmi fixed compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.

Consider the following statements:
1. Ujjawala (2007) covers prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
2. Ujjawala now functions as Shakti Sadan under the Sambal component of Mission Shakti.
3. One Stop Centres (Sakhi), funded by the Nirbhaya Fund, function from 1 April 2015.
4. District Anti-Human Trafficking Units work under an SP/DSP.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Shakti Sadan is under Samarthya, not Sambal.
